paper.title: New venture team stability and long-run organizational growth
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement is printed. The paper states only that it uses 'Danish register-based matched employer-employee data constructed by Statistics Denmark' (p. …

registers.name_in_paper: Danish register-based matched employer-employee data constructed by Statistics Denmark
registers.role: sample frame, treatment, outcome, controls and linkage: identifies all companies and all employees, allows new ventures and their founding teams to be identified and followed

registers.name_in_paper: register data on households and on deaths of NVT members and of their children, fathers and mothers (not named as a separate register)
registers.role: instruments: Presence of family relations, Own death in NVT, Child death in NVT, Father death in NVT, Mother death in NVT

linkages: companies and individuals matched with unique identifiers and traced over time
NVT members linked to the other founding members living in the same household at the time of startup
NVT members linked to their own death and to the deaths of their children, fathers and mothers in the first 3 years after founding
NVT members linked to their pre-founding employment history, past income, education and prior entrepreneurial experience from register years before the founding year t

sample.universe: All companies (including new ventures) and all employees in Denmark between 1980 and 2007; new ventures are companies that operate in year t but not in year t-1
sample.unit_of_observation: new venture (one record per venture, defined by its new venture team at founding)
selection_rules: identify new ventures as companies that operate in year t but not in year t-1
remove all firms with IDs that were used repeatedly, because firm IDs may be reused after a firm closes (endnote 2)
select all new ventures established between 1980 and 1997 and follow them for 10 years
drop 1980, which is used to construct variables reflecting past experiences for NVT members in 1981
end the sample in 1997 because of a data break 10 years later, in 2007
keep NVTs of size 2, 3 and 4 (67,138 ventures; 65.86% of new team-based ventures and 29.33% of all new ventures)
restrict to firms surviving three or more years, because NVT stability is constructed from mobility in the first 3 years: 37,401 ventures, 56% of the previous sample, the main regression sample
for Table 8, columns 2 and 3, drop founding years 1981-1983 because three years of history are needed to construct prior entrepreneurial experience: 30,198 ventures
for Figure 2, draw a larger sample covering the predominant range of founding team sizes, 2-10
sample.period: ventures founded 1981-1997, each followed for 10 years; register data 1980-2007
sample.n_observations: 37,401 (main regression sample); 67,138 before the three-year survival restriction; 30,198 in the 1984-1997 subsample

construction_notes: The NVT is defined as all individuals working for the new venture at the time of founding: membership requires neither equity, nor a formal title, nor involvement in strategy development.
NVT stability is operationalized over the 3 years after founding; the paper calls the 3-year window an empirical choice not grounded in theory and reports 2-year and 4-year alternatives in endnote 4.

Degree of NVT stability = proportion of NVT members still with the company after 3 years (1 if intact, 0 if all have left, e.g. 3/4, 2/4, 1/4 for a four-person team). Mean 0.45, SD 0.35, mode 0.5; 17% of NVTs remain completely intact and 27% have lost all members.
Intactness of NVT stability = dummy for an intact team after 3 years (mean 0.17, SD 0.38).
Duration of NVT stability = number of years the NVT remains intact, 0-3 (mean 0.85, SD 1.16).

Size10 = number of employees 10 years after founding, zero for ventures that did not survive; mean 2.81, SD 7.73. Average NVT size at founding is 2.70 (SD 0.78); 46% of ventures are still in operation in year 10; average size in year 3 conditional on survival is 4.34 and in year 10 conditional on survival 6.08.

Team member characteristics (age, gender, education, experience in years, sector experience, prior entrepreneurial experience, prior shared work experience, employment history, past income) are built from register years before the founding year t; venture characteristics including industry and founding team size come from year t.
Prior entrepreneurial experience = dummy for a NVT whose members had an entrepreneurial experience in the 3 years before the current venture was established; true for 15.56% of the sample.

Instrument frequencies in the regression sample: 9.80% of ventures have individuals from the same household at founding, 1.34% experience the death of a NVT member in the first 3 years, 6.30% a member losing a father, 3.36% a member losing a mother, 0.30% a member losing a child.

The 'representative' venture used for all simulated quantities is defined as a venture with average and mode sample characteristics; it has a degree of NVT stability of 0.5, an average education level of 10.88 years, an expected 10-year survival probability of 41.03% and an expected size conditional on survival of 9.05.
No deflation, winsorizing or currency conversion is described; the outcome is a headcount.

claims.statement: In a conventional (non-instrumented) Tobit model, the degree of NVT stability has a positive and significant effect on the size of the new venture 10 years after founding.

definition.value: The proportion of new venture team (NVT) members who are still with the company 3 years after founding: 1 if the NVT is intact after 3 years, 0 if all members have left, and intermediate values (e.g. 3/4, 2/4, 1/4 for a four-person NVT) in between. Mean 0.45, SD 0.35, mode 0.5.

timing.value: constructed over the first 3 years after founding

definition.value: The size of the new venture (number of employees) 10 years after founding; it is bounded below by zero, taking the value 0 for new ventures that did not survive to year 10. Sample mean 2.81, SD 7.73.

units.value: employees (number of persons employed by the venture in year 10) per one-unit increase in the stability variable

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional independence: given the control variables and the year and municipality fixed effects, NVT stability is unrelated to the unobserved determinants of the outcome. The paper does not claim this; it treats NVT stability as potentially endogenous and reports this specification only as a comparison.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper notes that the instrumented estimate is 'slightly smaller in magnitude but qualitatively similar', which it reads as evidence that endogeneity is minor.

ambiguities: Table 9 prints the two bounds but not their difference, and no standard error, confidence interval or significance test for the difference; the difference reported here is the arithmetic difference of the two printed values.
The row does not print an observation count.

The Table 9 row is printed as 'NVT stability (6 years window)'. It is read here as the time perspective of the OUTCOME (predicted survival to, and size in, year 6), because the paper calls rows 4-6 'different time perspectives' and because the predicted survival probabilities fall monotonically with the window length (0.710 at 4, 0.483 at 6, 0.392 at 8, 0.323 at 10 years). The alternative reading, that the window is the period over which NVT stability itself is constructed, cannot be ruled out from the printed table. The row also does not state which of the three stability measures it uses.
The intro states that an effect of stability emerges from 6 years after founding and increases in strength with more time; Table 9 itself reports no test of the difference.

evidence.how: The paper names no Statistics Denmark register or register variable: it describes its source only as 'Danish register-based matched employer-employee data constructed by Statistics Denmark' (p. 228). No DST register code or variable name is printed anywhere in the article.

The effect is the Table 9 upper-bound value for an intact NVT (0.623) minus the lower-bound value for a completely dissolved NVT (0.483) in the row 'NVT stability (6 years window)': 0.623 - 0.483 = 0.14. The paper prints the two bounds, not their difference, except in row 1 where the text states the difference.

Table 9 prints a standard deviation under each predicted value (0.141 for the lower bound, 0.123 for the upper bound) but no standard error, confidence interval or p-value for the difference between the two bounds.
No standard deviation of the outcome in the estimation sample is printed for this predicted quantity; the parenthesised numbers are the standard deviations of the two predictions themselves.
Table 9 prints no observation count for any of its rows; the underlying baseline rows rest on the main regression sample of 37,401 ventures.

ambiguities: Table 9 prints the two bounds but not their difference, and no standard error, confidence interval or significance test for the difference; the difference reported here is the arithmetic difference of the two printed values.
The row does not print an observation count.

The Table 9 row is printed as 'NVT stability (8 years window)'. It is read here as the time perspective of the OUTCOME (predicted survival to, and size in, year 8), because the paper calls rows 4-6 'different time perspectives' and because the predicted survival probabilities fall monotonically with the window length (0.710 at 4, 0.483 at 6, 0.392 at 8, 0.323 at 10 years). The alternative reading, that the window is the period over which NVT stability itself is constructed, cannot be ruled out from the printed table. The row also does not state which of the three stability measures it uses.
The intro states that an effect of stability emerges from 6 years after founding and increases in strength with more time; Table 9 itself reports no test of the difference.

evidence.how: The paper names no Statistics Denmark register or register variable: it describes its source only as 'Danish register-based matched employer-employee data constructed by Statistics Denmark' (p. 228). No DST register code or variable name is printed anywhere in the article.

The effect is the Table 9 upper-bound value for an intact NVT (10.506) minus the lower-bound value for a completely dissolved NVT (9.386) in the row 'NVT stability (8 years window)': 10.506 - 9.386 = 1.12. The paper prints the two bounds, not their difference, except in row 1 where the text states the difference.

Table 9 prints a standard deviation under each predicted value (1.223 for the lower bound, 1.305 for the upper bound) but no standard error, confidence interval or p-value for the difference between the two bounds.
No standard deviation of the outcome in the estimation sample is printed for this predicted quantity; the parenthesised numbers are the standard deviations of the two predictions themselves.
Table 9 prints no observation count for any of its rows; the underlying baseline rows rest on the main regression sample of 37,401 ventures.

claims.statement: Raising the average education of the new venture team from its sample average of 10.88 years to 12 years raises the representative venture's predicted size in year 10 conditional on survival by 0.17 employees, from 9.05 to 9.22.

treatment.label: Average years of education in the NVT

definition.value: The average education level of the NVT members in years; the “representative” venture has an average of 10.88 years, 12 years corresponds to completing high school and 17 years to a master's degree.

timing.value: measured in the founding year t from register data

outcome.label: Predicted firm size conditional on survival, E(Size10 | Size10 > 0)

definition.value: The Tobit-implied expected number of employees in year 10 conditional on the venture surviving, evaluated for the “representative” venture at the lower bound (completely dissolved NVT) and the upper bound (intact NVT) of the stability variable.

units.value: employees (persons) in year 10, conditional on survival

magnitude.interpretation: increase firm size by 0.17 employees (2 percent)

estimand.target_population: the 'representative' venture -- a venture with average and mode sample characteristics
estimand.time_horizon: predicted outcome 10 years after founding
estimand.formal_query: E[Predicted firm size conditional on survival, E(Size10 | Size10 > 0) | average NVT education = 12] - E[Predicted firm size conditional on survival, E(Size10 | Size10 > 0) | average NVT education = 10.88] for the 'representative' venture -- a venture with average and mode sample characteristics

population.description: New ventures established in Denmark between 1981 and 1997 whose new venture team (all individuals working for the venture at founding) had 2, 3 or 4 members, restricted to ventures surviving three or more years.
population.period: ventures founded 1981-1997, each followed for 10 years (register data 1980-2007)
subgroups_defined: NVT size 2, 3, 4
all-male / mixed-gender / all-female teams
NVT average education below / above the median
NVT with / without prior entrepreneurial experience
population.selection: Conditioned on survival to at least three years after founding (37,401 of the 67,138 ventures with NVT size 2-4, i.e. 56%), because NVT stability is measured over the first 3 years.

identification.source_of_variation: Variation in the average years of education of the new venture team across ventures, holding the other characteristics of the representative venture fixed; education enters the instrumented Tobit as a control variable and is not itself instrumented.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional independence: given the control variables and the year and municipality fixed effects, NVT stability is unrelated to the unobserved determinants of the outcome. The paper does not claim this; it treats NVT stability as potentially endogenous and reports this specification only as a comparison.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper notes that the instrumented estimate is 'slightly smaller in magnitude but qualitatively similar', which it reads as evidence that endogeneity is minor.

key_assumptions.assumption: Functional form: the outcome is the censoring at zero of a latent linear index, Tobit errors are additively separable and normally distributed, and NVT stability enters the latent index linearly.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper argues the Tobit suits the data structure (no upper limit, bounded below by zero, regressors observed for all ventures) and shows that Heckman, OLS and Poisson alternatives are qualitatively similar.

formal.as_written: Size10 = max{0, β * NVT Stability^ + X'γ + u1}

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on the venture surviving at least three years after founding, because NVT stability is constructed from mobility in the first 3 years; the estimate therefore holds only among ventures that reach year 3.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The restriction itself is stated (37,401 of 67,138 ventures, 56%), but the paper does not test or discuss the selection it induces.

implies_edges.from: Survival of the venture to at least 3 years after founding

key_assumptions.assumption: The simulated quantities are evaluated at a single covariate profile, the 'representative' venture -- a venture with average and mode sample characteristics, with only average NVT education varied; the effect reported is the effect for that profile.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper defines the representative venture and states that it simulates the effect of education by varying the average education level from 9 to 17 years.
